query: Why is learning satisfaction low for certain groups, and which factors drive it?

per_column.name: subject_format_alignment
per_column.rationale: Alignment between subject and delivery format is a candidate cause whose effect on satisfaction can be attributed; a plausible driver.

per_column.name: hands_on_requirement
per_column.rationale: The degree to which a subject needs hands-on work plausibly affects both format alignment (treatment) and satisfaction, making it a common cause worth adjusting for.

per_column.name: peer_interaction_impact
per_column.rationale: Peer interaction is itself a candidate driver of satisfaction/engagement; framed as impact on engagement it reads more as a treatment/mediator than a common cause.

per_column.name: teacher_instructional_adaptation
per_column.rationale: How much the teacher adapts instruction is another candidate cause of satisfaction rather than a common cause of another treatment.

per_column.name: family_support_availability
per_column.rationale: Family support capacity plausibly affects both student engagement/exposure to adapted instruction and satisfaction; a genuine background common cause surfaced from data, not on the causal path itself.

per_column.name: student_prior_engagement
per_column.rationale: Baseline/prior engagement plausibly drives both current teacher adaptation received and later satisfaction, and precedes the treatments, so it is a pre-treatment common cause rather than a mediator.

judge.rationale: The query names no specific factors, so every added column is surfaced rather than copied. The set supplies clear candidate treatments (subject_format_alignment, teacher_instructional_adaptation, peer_interaction_impact) and several plausible background common causes (student_prior_engagement, family_support_availability, and to a lesser extent hands_on_requirement) that precede or drive both treatments and satisfaction. This realises a genuine causal-attribution setup: treatment(s) plus non-query-named confounders. The main weakness is that some columns (peer_interaction_impact) are framed in outcome-tainted terms and blur the treatment/mediator line, so confounder quality is good but not excellent.
